### Recommended Non-Vegetarian Dinner Spots in Tokyo (Under JPY 3,000 / Dish)

---

### 1. Gyukatsu Motomura (牛かつ もと村)
*Branches across Tokyo including Shibuya, Shinjuku, and Akihabara*  
**Website:** [Gyukatsu Motomura](https://www.gyukatsu-motomura.com/)

A specialty chain dedicated to deep-fried beef cutlets (*gyukatsu*). Each diner receives a mini stone grill at the table to sear each rare-cooked slice to their preferred doneness.

* **Gyukatsu Set Meal (1 Cutlet / 130g) – JPY 1,930 – JPY 2,110** (portion-based set)  
  *Ingredients & Preparation:* Beef loin coated in a thin panko breadcrumb batter, quick-fried rare and pre-sliced. Served with barley rice (*mugimeshi*), miso soup, shredded cabbage, potato salad, pickles, grated yam (*tororo*), and spicy cod roe (*mentaiko*).
* **Gyukatsu Set Meal (1.5 Cutlets / 195g) – JPY 2,600** (listed portion set)  
  *Ingredients & Preparation:* 195 grams of breaded, rare-fried beef cutlets served with the full set of side dishes, sauces (wasabi soy and horseradish), and rice.

* **Diner Feedback:**
  * *Positive:* Diners love the interactive personal hot stone and the melt-in-the-mouth tenderness of the beef.
  * *Negative / Caveats:* Wait times during peak dinner hours routinely range between 45 and 90 minutes.

---

### 2. Tonkatsu Tonki (とんかつ とんき 目黒本店)
*1-1-2 Shimomeguro, Meguro-ku, Tokyo*  
**Venue / Guide Link:** [AutoReserve Tonkatsu Tonki](https://autoreserve.com/restaurants/Q3yWvXm7V)

Operating in Meguro since 1939, this institution is famous for its open kitchen counter and distinct frying style, producing cutlets coated in a dark, crisp crust.

* **Rosu-Katsu Teishoku (ロースかつ定食) – JPY 2,300** (listed set price)  
  *Ingredients & Preparation:* Thick pork loin dipped repeatedly in flour and egg, rolled in fine panko, and slow-fried in pure lard. Served with tonjiru (pork miso soup), rice, pickles, and finely shredded cabbage.
* **Hire-Katsu Teishoku (ヒレかつ定食) – JPY 2,300** (listed set price)  
  *Ingredients & Preparation:* Lean, tender pork tenderloin/fillet prepared with the same signature crisp coating, accompanied by unlimited refills of cabbage and tonjiru soup.
* **Kushikatsu Set (串かつ定食) – JPY 1,600 – JPY 1,800** (a la carte skewer JPY 1,100)  
  *Ingredients & Preparation:* Skewered pork cuts paired with green onion/sweet onion, breaded and fried crisp.

* **Diner Feedback:**
  * *Positive:* Highly praised for generous, complimentary refills of pork soup and cabbage, as well as the theatrical, synchronized kitchen counter service.
  * *Negative / Caveats:* The batter separates readily from the meat (a signature feature of Tonki's technique that not all modern tonkatsu fans enjoy), and waiting lines can exceed an hour.

---

### 3. Torigin Ginza Honten (銀座 鳥ぎん 本店)
*B1F, New Ginza Bldg 6, 5-5-7 Ginza, Chuo-ku, Tokyo*  
**Official Menu:** [Torigin Ginza English Menu](https://torigin-ginza.jp/en/)

Founded in 1951, Torigin specializes in authentic binchotan-grilled chicken skewers (*yakitori*) and traditional iron-pot rice casseroles (*kamameshi*).

* **Tori Kamameshi (鳥釜めし) – JPY 1,050 – JPY 1,200** (listed menu price)  
  *Ingredients & Preparation:* Raw Japanese rice simmered in an individual iron pot over open flame with diced seasoned chicken, chicken broth, and shiitake mushrooms, forming a savory crust (*okoge*) at the base.
* **Gomoku Kamameshi (五目釜めし) – JPY 1,350 – JPY 1,500** (listed menu price)  
  *Ingredients & Preparation:* Iron-pot rice steamed with ground chicken mince, bamboo shoots, shrimp, crab, and shiitake mushrooms.
* **Yakitori Skewer Selection (5–8 Skewer Set) – JPY 990 – JPY 1,800** (per skewer: JPY 200–260)  
  *Ingredients & Preparation:* Japanese chicken thigh, scallion-chicken (*negima*), minced chicken meatballs (*tsukune*), and liver basted in tare (sweet soy glaze) or sprinkled with sea salt and grilled over binchotan charcoal.

* **Diner Feedback:**
  * *Positive:* Excellent value for prime Ginza dining; skewers are juicy and smoky, and the pot-cooked rice is deeply comforting.
  * *Negative / Caveats:* Kamameshi is cooked strictly from raw rice upon ordering and takes 15–25 minutes to arrive at the table.

---

### Recommendation & Practical Tips
* For quick dining with minimal queueing, arrive around 17:00 at either **Tonkatsu Tonki** (opens at 16:00) or **Gyukatsu Motomura**. 
* At **Torigin**, order your *kamameshi* rice pot at the exact same time as your skewers so it finishes cooking just as you conclude your yakitori course.
